text:
A few days after one Montreal outlet ran the headline "'He cost them the game'" about Jacob Fowler, the rookie goalie went into Scotiabank Arena and stole one. Fowler stopped 26 of 28 shots, about 1.6 goals better than the chances he faced, and the Canadiens beat the Maple Leafs 4-2. Toronto was the better team by our numbers, and it didn't matter.

Alex Newhook gave Montreal its cushion in the first period, scoring at 5:56 off an Oliver Kapanen feed and again at 13:06 on a tip. Chris Kreider made it 3-0 midway through the second, unassisted, during the period Toronto controlled most clearly: the Leafs out-chanced Montreal 1.40 to 0.55 in expected goals (the quality of chances) in the second and came away with nothing. That is where Fowler won the game.

The Leafs finally broke through early in the third. William Nylander hammered a power-play slap shot in at 6:19, and Gavin McKenna, the teenager whose first weeks in Toronto have filled the headlines, scored 55 seconds later to make it 3-2. By our win probability model, McKenna's goal was the biggest swing of the night, lifting Toronto from 7 percent to 23.

Montreal ended it the way good road teams do. Zachary Bolduc scored on a power-play slap shot at 12:15, and later the Canadiens killed off a Juraj Slafkovsky double minor, which The Hockey News' Karine Hains called a huge kill. Sergei Bobrovsky allowed four on 28, about 1.4 worse than expected, though he did stop Cole Caufield on a 32 percent chance in the third.

Overall the Leafs had 64 shot attempts to 50 and 3.56 expected goals to 2.95, and our numbers say they deserved to win 66 percent of the time. They are now winless in four Atlantic Division games (0-3-1), per The Leafs Nation, which summed up the night as Toronto continuing "to master the fake comeback." For Montreal, with Nick Suzuki back in the lineup and Ivan Demidov making progress from his injury, a goalie who just took a public beating looks a lot more like the guy Sportsnet's Eric Engels has been writing about in the same breath as Carey Price.
headline: Fowler answers his critics as Habs win in Toronto
